request.system:
You check whether short claims are faithful to the source texts they cite.

The claims form one answer and are read together: a condition or exception stated in another claim does not need to be repeated, and a claim that summarises part of a text is faithful if that part is accurate. Mark a claim unfaithful only when it asserts something the cited texts contradict or do not support.

For each claim, answer: does the claim follow from the cited texts alone, without adding, narrowing, or changing anything they say? A claim that paraphrases or restates accurately is faithful — identical wording is not required. A claim that introduces a number, condition, or conclusion the texts do not support is not. Each cited text is labelled with its reference (e.g. "3.A.6") and title; a claim may use that label. Judge only the substance of the claim against its texts; ignore whether it answers any particular question and ignore framing about what a text is or is not about. Give a one-sentence reason.

verdicts.reason: Classification as fee-paying or not turns on the fee schedule per 1.D.6, and 3.A.2 only says non-fee-paying may be included, so the texts settle only part of the inclusion question.
1.D.6 says a portfolio subject to the fee schedule is fee-paying whether or not the fee is reduced or waived in whole or in part.
Since waiver in whole does not change fee-paying status under 1.D.6, a full waiver alone does not make an account non-fee-paying.

1.D.6 implies portfolios not subject to the fee schedule are not fee-paying, and 3.A.2 permits inclusion of non-fee-paying discretionary portfolios; the discretionary condition is stated in 3.A.2 context but the claim is reasonably consistent.
3.A.2 says non-fee-paying portfolios 'may be included', indicating optional inclusion.
3.A.2 states that where included, the firm must disclose the percentage at each annual period end.
3.A.2 text refers only to non-fee-paying discretionary portfolios, so it addresses only discretionary ones.
1.D.5 states a portfolio is discretionary when the firm has sufficient authority to implement its intended strategy.
1.D.5 requires firms to document the basis for each determination that restrictions render a portfolio non-discretionary.
Neither 1.D.6 nor 1.D.1 contains any requirement to include fee-paying discretionary portfolios in a composite; they are only definitions.
The cited definitions contain no mandatory inclusion rule, so mandatory inclusion for fee-paying accounts cannot be confirmed from them.
